verses.1: And the LORD spoke to Moses, saying:
verses.2: I speak to the children of Israel, and I say to them: No man or woman shall be allowed to become a priest or a leader in the service of Jehovah.
verses.3: One day, and the reward will be given to those who work hard. But all those who do not work hard will not receive any reward. And all those who harvest ripe fruits will not be able to eat them.
verses.4: All the days of Nizro are spent on all that is made from grape juice, from raisins and other ingredients. But nothing of this can be eaten at all.
verses.5: Every day of Nedar, it will be a time when no one can pass by his head until the days are complete. Then, when Jehovah’s holiness is fulfilled, his head will grow taller.
verses.6: Every day that one serves the LORD, they will never die.
verses.7: To his father and mother, to his brothers and sisters, they shall not be buried in the grave, for their God has honored them above all others.
verses.8: All the days of Nizro are holy to Jehovah.
verses.9: And in a sudden and unexpected manner, he died. His head was shaved off on the day of his purification. On the seventh day, his head was shaved off.
verses.10: And on the eighth day, two young men, or two sons of Yona, went to the priest at the entrance of the Tabernacle.
verses.11: And one priest made a sacrifice for sin, and another for holiness. He covered the head with a covering as a sign of his sin. Then he sanctified his head on that day.
verses.12: And he shall bring Jehovah’s days of judgment. He will bring back the son of his youth to Assyria. But those early days will be ruined, because Nizro is a wicked man.
verses.13: And this is the rule for a monk on the day when his monastic life comes to an end. He will be brought before the door of the temple.
verses.14: And he offered his lamb to the LORD. It was a pure one, one year old. And another lamb, a pure one, from its second year, was also offered as an offering for sin. And one pure grain was also offered as an offering for offerings.
verses.15: And the spices are mixed with honey. The spices themselves are also mixed with honey, and then they are cooked together.
verses.16: And the priest brought him forward before Yahweh, and he atoned for his sin and his transgressions.
verses.17: And he shall make an offering of sacrifices to Jehovah on the altar of offerings. And the priest shall prepare his offering and his food for the sacrifice.
verses.18: And when the priest cut off the head of the priest’s offering, he took the hair from the head of the offering and placed it on the fire that was beneath the burnt offerings.
verses.19: And the priest took some seeds from the field. He also took one of the stalks from the crop, and one of the leaves. Then he placed these on the shoulders of the priest after he had shaved off his beard.
verses.20: And the priest shall raise them up in front of Jehovah, the Holy One. He shall do this in front of the ark of the covenant and on top of the altar. After that, the priest shall pour holy oil over them.
verses.21: This is the rule for the monk who brings his sacrifice to God. He should do this by placing his hand in a position that resembles that of a sacrifice. This is how he must perform his ritual.
verses.22: And Jehovah spoke to Moses, saying:
verses.23: I said to Aaron and his sons, “Bless the children of Israel.”
verses.24: May Jehovah bless you and protect you.
verses.25: May the LORD’s face be with you, and may He bless you.
verses.26: May the LORD bring His face towards you, and may He grant you peace.
verses.27: And they have written my name on the children of Israel. I will bless them.
